The Strait of Hormuz As Trump's Asset. Why the War Again? 

🔤🔤🔤🔤➖

Trump has said that the United States will charge a 20 percent fee on cargo shipped through the Strait of Hormuz, despite his own administration’s position that such fees violate international law.

He made the announcement on Monday amid an intensifying battle between Iran and the United States to control the waterway, a crucial artery for global energy supplies. 

The two countries have traded attacks over the strait for the past week, in effect shattering their month-old cease-fire.

Since the U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iran in February that set off the war, Iran has periodically fired on commercial ships transiting the strait as it seeks to compel vessels to use a route close to its coast, a potential precursor to charging its own fees.

In announcing his plan to levy a toll, the president described it as a way for the United States to recover the cost of providing military protection to vessels using the waterway.

“The Hormuz Strait is OPEN, and will remain OPEN, with or without Iran,” Trump wrote on social media. He added that the United States would levy the 20 percent fee for “any and all costs necessary,” describing it as “a matter of FAIRNESS,” and also said the United States would resume a blockade of Iranian ports.

This is not the first time Trump has threatened such a toll. He raised the possibility last month after signing a temporary cease-fire agreement with Iran, even though that deal included language that Tehran has interpreted to mean it has authority over the strait. 

The memorandum also said that no country would collect tolls for 60 days, though it left open the possibility for such charges beyond that.

This isn’t exactly clear. Trump did not elaborate on how the 20 percent fee would be calculated or how it would be collected.

Trump and his aides also have not explained why his position contradicts the assertions of top officials in his administration.

Addressing the people of Jordan, the IRGC said that a significant portion of US military operations against Iran had been launched from American bases on Jordanian territory.
​
The IRGC called on Jordanians to end the presence of US forces in their country and prevent its territory from being used as a launchpad for attacks against Islamic nations and the Palestinian people. ​
In a separate statement, the IRGC said its Navy had targeted the US Fifth Fleet’s facilities in Bahrain, striking the NSI management center, the command and control center, large warehouses containing military parts and equipment, and fuel storage facilities.
​
The IRGC said the strikes in Bahrain were in response to the United States’ deploying its naval forces in the Indian Ocean and blocking maritime routes under the pretext of controlling the Strait of Hormuz, which had disrupted the region’s oil and gas exports.
​
“The enemy should know that now that its pirates have blocked the Indian Ocean route for the export of the region’s oil and gas to the world—a move that endangers the interests of America’s economic rivals—it must expect other oil and gas export routes that serve the interests of the United States and its allies to be closed as well,” the IRGC warned, saying: “The region’s oil and gas exports will either be available to everyone or to no one.”

🎙 IRGC declares strikes on US military facilities in Kuwait during Operation Nasr-2

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) announces that it has carried out a new wave of missile and drone strikes targeting US military facilities in Kuwait, saying several strategic installations were destroyed as part of the ongoing Operation Nasr-2 (Victory-2).

In separate statements released early Wednesday, the IRGC said its Aerospace Force and Ground Force launched the fourth and sixth waves of the operation in retaliation for recent US attacks on targets in Iran.
​
According to the statements, the strikes targeted the KJL facility, the primary logistics and supply hub for US forces across West Asia, in Mina Abdullah, Kuwait, which the IRGC said was set on fire and destroyed.
​
It also asserted that missile and drone attacks struck a US satellite communications center, missile defense and air defense radar systems, a Patriot air defense complex, military logistics facilities, and HIMARS missile launch platforms stationed in Kuwait.
​
The IRGC described the measures as a response to US military operations against Iranian territory.
​
In one of the statements, the IRGC directly addressed the people of Kuwait, stressing that Iran had no hostility toward the Kuwaiti nation and that the attacks were aimed solely at American military forces operating from bases in the country.
​
It urged Kuwaitis to seek the removal of US troops from their territory, arguing that foreign military bases had become the source of attacks against Iran.
​
The IRGC also reiterated that its retaliatory operations would continue and announced that the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until US aggression comes to an end.
